messages:
maria_g: Hey team — hitting a weird perf dip on FP8 on H100 in the canary fleet. Latency p95 up ~25% vs L40S for same load. Telemetry shows an unexpected spike in sampling events. Can we quick-check kernel selection telemetry?

jon_m: Do you have the perf counters / sample dump? batch sizes and kv-hit rates?

maria_g: Quick paste from the canary snapshot (rolled-up):
```
sample_rate_reported: 0.01
sample_events_observed: 0.12
kernel_choice: FP8_TE_FASTPATH (72%), INT8_FALLBACK (28%)
avg_latency_ms: 48
p95_latency_ms: 134
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.63
batch_size_avg: 4.6
```
Looks like we only set sampling to 1% but observed events are ~12% — seems correlated with fastpath on H100.

perf-bot: Profiling job queued: job=pf-2524681357-03, sampling=1%, targets=h100-canary

eli_w: That sounds like the telemetry sampler drift I warned about. Last week's change incremented the TE fastpath log counter per-request (we incremented inside the microbatch loop). Could inflate observed samples on faster kernels.

maria_g: Ah — yes, I see the incr code in `transformer_engine/logging.cc` doing `sampler.record()` inside the kv-warmup loop. On H100 fastpaths that loop runs N times per token so sampler gets Nx hits.

kevin_p: That explains the selector bias. Kernel selector uses recent telemetry frequency to weight heuristics. If sampling is over-counted on H100 FP8, selector thinks FP8 is more stable/performant and routes more there, creating a feedback loop and causing p95 jitter when workload mixes long contexts. We should decouple raw sampler event counts from selector inputs (use normalized rates).

rachel_t: Short mitigation: cap telemetry weight in kernel selector to a smoothed rate and ignore >5% instantaneous jumps. I prepared a tiny patch to clamp sample counts before feeding selectors — PR: https://phabricator.redwood/CL/PR-9999 (canary-only toggle)

jon_m: Repro steps to validate?

maria_g: 1) deploy canary with patch flag on
2) run perf-runner seq len 1024, batch=8, mix=50/50 recurrent/static
3) collect `kernel_choice` and p95 over 10m

kevin_p: Also change TE config: `te_kern_sel_mode=stable` and set `te_telemetry_per_request=false` (defaults to true now). That avoids per-microbatch sampling.

maria_g: Rolled both changes to canary just now. Quick metric after ~6m: p95 down to 103ms, avg 42ms, kernel_choice FP8 58% / INT8 42% (more balanced), sample_events_observed normalized to 0.011.
```
post_patch_p95_ms: 103
post_patch_avg_ms: 42
post_patch_kv_hit: 0.64
post_patch_sample_rate: 0.011
```

perf-bot: Canary deploy succeeded: pf-2524681357-03 -> healthy

eli_w: Nice. Follow-up: add unit test that ensures sampler increment is only called once per request (not per microbatch) and add e2e that compares per-hardware normalized sample rates.

rachel_t: I'll take the PR and add the cap + test, then land to stable if green.

maria_g: Thanks all — I'll open a short RFC to split telemetry (observability) and selector inputs (policy) so future sampling changes don't leak into routing heuristics. Will include a small experiment plan to test FP8/INT8/4-bit on both H100/L40S under synthetic skew. :rocket:
